theater: 上秘魯高原與玻利維亞礦區

battle.name: 玻利維亞獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 上秘魯高原與玻利維亞礦區
battle.brief: 一八〇九年五月起，蘇克雷斯與拉巴斯先後舉義，上秘魯礦區民兵與西班牙王軍在安第斯高原對峙。卡面這門可拆成幾件車體、由馬匹牽引的野砲，正是王軍野戰砲隊的骨幹：它隨砲車隊行進，在高原隘口以實心彈與霰彈壓住缺乏火炮的起義民兵。整場戰爭打到一八二四年才在阿亞庫喬分出勝負。

kit.name: 野砲
kit.history: 能拆成幾件馬車拉走的砲。它讓野戰第一次有了可以計算的砲火。

countries: 交戰的一方是西班牙王室在安的黎斯治理下的秘魯總督府：利馬的總督霍阿金·德·拉·佩蘇埃拉自一八〇九年接掌最高軍政權，透過王室法庭與上秘魯各區的 corregidor、comandante de armas 分層控制波托西、蘇克雷斯與拉巴斯三個行政中心，駐軍由佩內陸軍師與皇家砲兵隊組成，並大量徵召原住民兵團（例如以克丘亞、艾馬拉兵為主的肯迪團）守備城鎮、護送銀礦。另一方是起義者：五月十日在蘇克雷斯召開市議會奪權後成立的自治執政會，七月十六日拉巴斯起義後成立的第二個執政會，兩者麾下由鎮上的攤販、鞋匠、織工、礦工與鄉村原住民組成的民兵，以及在查奇亞與永加斯山區活動的瓜拉尼與契里瓜諾部落游擊隊。雙方指揮系統本質不同：西班牙方有標準的營制、砲隊與後勤；起義方以執政會為最高權，靠臨時徵召與群眾動員運作，人數多而編制鬆散，且因克里奧爾菁英與純血原住民利益不一、城市與鄉村分屬不同執政會，協調極差。
countriesEn: The Spanish side was the Viceroyalty of Peru, then ruled for the Crown from Madrid: Viceroy Joaquín de la Pezuela took supreme civil and military authority in 1809 and governed the three administrative centres of Potosí, Chuquisaca and La Paz through the Audiencia, the district corregidores and the comandantes de armas. His field forces came from peninsular line regiments and the Royal Artillery (Real Cuerpo de Artillería), heavily reinforced with indigenous battalions such as the Kendi regiment, drawn largely from Quechua and Aymara soldiers, who garrisoned the towns and escorted the silver convoys. The other side was the insurgents: the autonomous junta created at Chuquisaca after the cabildo abierto of 10 May; the second junta formed after the La Paz rising of 16 July; the market sellers, shoemakers, weavers, miners and rural Indians enrolled as militias; and the Guaraní and Chiriguano bands that fought as guerrillas in the Chichas and Yungas uplands. The two command systems were fundamentally different. Spain had a standard establishment, an artillery brigade and a working supply service. The insurgents ran the war through juntas, improvised levies and mass mobilisation: numerous but loosely organised, and poorly coordinated, because creole and indigenous elites did not pull the same way and because the two cities answered to rival juntas.
people: 前驅是圖帕克·阿馬魯二世，即約瑟夫·加夫列爾·孔多爾坎基，一七八〇至一七八一年在上秘魯率領大規模原住民起義，一七八一年五月在拉巴斯被處決，遺體被肢解分別陳示於總督轄內各城，後人稱他為最後一位抗爭的印加人。一八〇九年五月七日拉巴斯先爆發抗稅暴動，起義者佩德羅·多明戈·穆里略被捕，十三日被斬首，四肢分送各城示眾；五月十日蘇克雷斯的 corregidor 弗朗西斯科·安東尼奧·德·塞拉尼加被市議會推翻，接任的胡安·德·迪奧斯·阿里斯佩後來主持一八一六年大河之普拉塔制憲會議。七月十六日拉巴斯攔截即將開往蘇克雷斯的肯迪團，中校安東尼奧·何塞·德·雷耶斯在廣場被殺；二十五日，何塞·曼努埃爾·德·利馬在守衛穆里略宅邸時陣亡。起義軍方面，蘇克雷斯執政會派出的混血上校格里戈里奧·帕切科率軍北上，在蒙特雷與聖維森特接連失利，一八一〇年五月被處決。皇家軍方面，除佩蘇埃拉總督外，另有在高地指揮皇家部隊的蒙泰阿古多侯爵，以及一八一三至一八一四年在比爾卡班巴打垮克丘科義軍的何塞·曼努埃爾·德·戈伊內切。一八二四年，玻利瓦爾與安東尼奧·何塞·德·蘇亞雷斯在胡寧與阿亞庫喬完成最後一擊。
peopleEn: The precursor was Túpac Amaru II, José Gabriel Condorcanqui, who led a vast indigenous rising across Upper Peru in 1780 and 1781 and was executed in La Paz in May 1781, his body quartered and displayed in cities across the viceroyalty; later generations called him the last Inca resister. On 7 May 1809 La Paz erupted first in a riot against new taxes; the insurgent Pedro Domingo Murillo was arrested and beheaded on 13 May, his limbs sent to different cities as a warning. On 10 May the corregidor of Chuquisaca, Francisco Antonio de Zelañiga, was overthrown by the municipal council, and his successor Juan de Dios Arispe would later preside over the Assembly of the Río de la Plata in 1816. On 16 July La Paz intercepted the Kendi regiment on its way to Chuquisaca and killed its lieutenant colonel Antonio José de Reyes in the square; on the 25th José Manuel de Lima fell while defending the Murillo house. On the insurgent side Gregorio Pacheco, the mestizo colonel sent north by the Chuquisaca junta, was beaten at Monterrei and San Vicente and was executed in May 1810. On the royal side, besides Viceroy de la Pezuela, stood the marquis of Monteagudo, who commanded royal troops in the highlands, and José Manuel de Goyeneche, who crushed the Cuzco insurgents at Vilcabamba in 1813 and 1814. In 1824 Bolívar and Antonio José de Sucre struck the final blow at Junín and Ayacucho.
kits: 卡面這門野砲是一五五〇年前後西班牙已能拆成幾件車體、用馬匹牽引隨軍移動的野戰火砲；到一八〇九年，皇家砲兵隊使用的已是數代之後的製品：四磅、六磅與八磅野砲為野戰主力，十二磅砲與六磅、十二磅短管榴砲配在旅團一級，攻城用的十六至二十四磅重砲則留在後方堡壘。野砲連同前車與彈藥車構成可拆解的砲車隊，砲組通常五至八人，火藥與彈藥分裝成箱由騾馬馱運，因此皇家砲兵隊的推進速度由騾馬飼料與道路決定，遠不如步騎兵。起義方沒有成建制的砲兵：民兵使用燧發滑膛火槍與短管霰彈槍，配皮製彈盒、火繩、鐵矛與長矛（lanza），另有彈弓、木棒與斧；瓜拉尼與契里瓜諾的游擊隊則以弓矢與長矛奇襲商隊。與野砲火力最接近的，是起義軍在永加斯山區馬西亞爾·聖塔克魯斯一役攻破皇家軍哨所後繳獲的火器、馬匹與軍需，但那只是散落的失物，不構成炮兵單位。真正決定戰局的是皇家軍把野砲帶上高原：安第斯山道窄、坡陡、隘口成串，砲口一線排開便可封死通道，起義民兵一旦在開闊高地密集衝鋒，砲火與霰彈便成片收割，野砲遂成雙方火力差距的具體形狀。
kitsEn: The field gun on the card is the kind of Spanish artillery piece of around 1550 that could be broken down into cart bodies and towed by horses; by 1809 the Royal Artillery was firing pieces several generations later: four-, six- and eight-pounders as the field battery standard, twelve-pounders and short six- and twelve-pounder howitzers attached to the brigade, while the heavy sixteen- to twenty-four-pounder siege guns stayed in fortresses behind the lines. A field gun with its limber and caisson formed a column that could be broken down, the gun crew numbering usually five to eight men, with powder and shot travelling in boxes on mules; the pace of the royal artillery was therefore set by fodder and roads and was far below that of foot and horse. The insurgents had no organised artillery at all: the militias used flintlock smoothbore muskets and short blunderbusses, with leather cartridge boxes, powder flasks, iron-tipped lances (lanza), slings, clubs and axes, and the Guaraní and Chiriguano guerrillas used bows and lances to ambush convoys. The closest the insurgents came to field artillery was what they picked up after breaking into a royalist post at Mariscal Santa Cruz in the Yungas in August 1809, taking muskets, horses and stores, but that was scattered loot rather than an artillery unit. What actually decided the fighting was the royal artillery taking its guns up onto the plateau: Andean tracks are narrow, steep and threaded with passes, so a line of guns could seal a defile, and when insurgent militia charged in dense masses across open high ground, round shot and canister cut them down in ranks, so the field gun became the physical shape of the fire gap between the two sides.
tactics: 皇家軍以縱隊行軍，砲隊居中，步兵分列兩翼，騎兵在側翼與高地巡弋；進攻時先以野砲在遠程發射實心彈壓制，再以短管榴砲打擊密集隊形，逼近後才以霰彈與刺刀接戰。守方若據守山脊，砲兵會佔據高處反擊——一八〇九年十一月的聖維森特之戰就是典型：皇家軍把砲架在海拔近五千公尺的波托西山脊上，起義軍自山下低地以長矛與火槍密集攀援，屢次衝上又被砲火壓回，最後在正面火力差距下崩潰。起義方的戰術則是另一套：以市集攤販動員群眾，用石塊與木料在街道與屋舍之間築成街壘，據守要衝以火槍射擊，再以長矛與棍棒近身格鬥；七月十六日的拉巴斯之役正是靠街壘與巷戰拖住皇家軍的直線射擊，二十五日守衛穆里略宅邸亦然。鄉村方面，契里瓜諾游擊隊在山區切斷皇家軍的糧道與銀礦運輸線，令對方必須分兵護路。整體而言，起義方在狹隘地形與夜戰中尚有可為，一旦進入高原開闊地、必須正面承受野砲與騎兵衝擊，便無力支撐。此外，高原海拔三千六百至四千米，夜間嚴寒、日夜溫差大，乾季（五月至十一月）才是行軍與作戰季節，一旦入雨季，道路泥濘，砲車隊與騾馬後勤便成為最大弱點。
tacticsEn: The royal army marched in column, with the guns in the centre, infantry in two lines to the flanks and cavalry screening the sides and the heights. On the attack they opened with solid shot at long range, then used short howitzers to break up massed formations before closing to canister and bayonet. A defender holding a ridge was answered from above: the action at San Vicente in November 1809 is the type case, the royal guns emplaced on a ridge above Potosí at nearly five thousand metres while the insurgents climbed from the low ground below with lances and muskets, were driven back again and again by the gun fire, and finally collapsed under the frontal fire gap. The insurgents fought on a different logic. They mobilised the market sellers, built street barricades out of stones and timber between houses and streets, held the strong points with musket fire and met the assault at close quarters with lances and clubs; the La Paz rising of 16 July was won in exactly that way, with barricades and house-to-house fighting blunting the royalists' straight shooting, and again in the defence of the Murillo house on the 25th. In the countryside, Chiriguano guerrillas cut the royal supply and silver routes in the mountains, forcing the enemy to detach columns to guard them. In general the insurgents could still fight in defiles and at night, but once they were pushed onto open plateau and had to stand the shock of guns and cavalry they had nothing to hold with. Altitude added its own constraints: the plateau lies between three thousand six hundred and four thousand metres, the nights are hard frost and the diurnal swing is large, and the dry season from May to November is the campaigning season. Once the rains set in the roads turn to mud, and the gun train and the mule supply become the greatest weakness of any army in the mountains.
data: 可考的數字大致如下：波托西銀礦（Cerro Rico）位於海拔約四千零九十公尺，據礦業史研究，其十六至十九世紀間的白銀產量以萬噸計，常見估計在三千萬公斤上下；Huancavelica 的水銀礦約三千二百公尺，與波托西的銀礦同屬水銀冶煉法的兩端。白銀沿阿里的卡港經高原山道運出，港口到礦場的道路長約六百公里，屬當時世界上最難走的運兵路之一。全區海拔：拉巴斯約三千六百四十公尺、蘇克雷斯約二千七百九十公尺、波托西約四千零九十公尺；蘇克雷斯到拉巴斯公路約五百公里，波托西到蘇克雷斯約一百二十公里。砲兵技術參數亦有據可依：四磅彈約一點五公斤、六磅約二點二公斤、八磅約三公斤、十二磅約四點五公斤，野砲一門的砲組通常五至八人。日期方面：一七八〇至一七八一年圖帕克·阿馬魯起義；一八〇九年五月七日拉巴斯首次暴動、五月十日蘇克雷斯革命、五月十三日穆里略被處決、七月十六日拉巴斯革命、同日肯迪團被攔、八月永加斯山區的馬西亞爾·聖塔克魯斯之役、十月蘇克雷斯被皇家軍攻陷、十一月七日與十二月八日蒙特雷兩戰、十一月中聖維森特之役；其後一八一〇年五月拉巴斯第一共和國崩潰，一八一三年十月比爾卡班巴之役終結克丘科的抵抗，一八二四年十二月九日阿亞庫喬戰役。戰爭自一八〇九年延續到一八二四年，前後十五年，頭一年即已進入高原作戰季。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are roughly these. The silver mine of Cerro Rico at Potosí stands at about four thousand and ninety metres, and mining-history research puts its output between the sixteenth and nineteenth centuries in the tens of thousands of tonnes, a commonly cited estimate being around thirty million kilograms; the mercury workings of Huancavelica at about three thousand two hundred metres form the other end of the patio process. The silver left through the port of Arica over a plateau road of roughly six hundred kilometres, one of the hardest supply roads in the world at the time. Elevations across the theatre: La Paz about 3,640 metres, Chuquisaca about 2,790 metres, Potosí about 4,090 metres; the road from Chuquisaca to La Paz runs some five hundred kilometres, and from Potosí to Chuquisaca about a hundred and twenty. The artillery parameters are documented: a four-pounder ball weighs about 1.5 kilograms, the six-pounder 2.2, the eight-pounder 3, the twelve-pounder 4.5, and a field gun normally carried a crew of five to eight men. On dates: the Túpac Amaru rising of 1780 and 1781; the first La Paz riot of 7 May 1809; the Chuquisaca revolution of 10 May; Murillo's execution on 13 May; the La Paz rising of 16 July; the interception of the Kendi regiment the same day; the action at Mariscal Santa Cruz in the Yungas in August; the fall of Chuquisaca to the royalists in October; the two battles of Monterrei on 7 November and 8 December; the action at San Vicente in mid-November; then the collapse of the first republic at La Paz in May 1810, the end of Cuzco resistance at Vilcabamba in October 1813, and the battle of Ayacucho on 9 December 1824. The war ran from 1809 to 1824, fifteen years, and the first campaigning season on the plateau was already under way in the opening year.
cause: 起因是多層的。最遠的一層是制度：一八〇九年的上秘魯是帝國的經濟心臟，白銀與水銀的產量讓利馬與塞維利亞都離不開它，但它在政治上卻隸屬利馬的秘魯總督府與王室法庭，本地沒有自己的代議機構，十八世紀末四大王國的改革浪潮中，上秘魯被刻意留在改革之外，只保留了向總督府陳情、而非決定自身命運的權利。行政上，一七七六年總督曼努埃爾·德·阿馬特把波托西一帶從蘇克雷斯的管轄中劃出設為總督區，蘇克雷斯的市民階層因此認定自己的地盤與司法權被剝奪，這種不滿是五月十日革命直接的火種。短期的導火線是西班牙王權的崩解：一八〇八年拿破崙侵入伊比利亞，舊王室退位，克里奧爾菁英自組忠貞王國議會號召效忠波旁，而秘魯總督府內部在效忠問題上本身分歧叢生，一八〇八年十一月阿班凱的商人起義被武力鎮壓並有數人被處決，更令上秘魯的菁英與百姓對總督府的治理能力失去信心。最後是結構性的怨恨：銀礦仰賴 mita 勞役制度年年從高原各村抽走大量年輕勞動力，契里瓜諾與瓜拉尼聚落還要承受土地與人口安置的壓力，於是當起義的消息傳到山區，這些社群毫不猶豫地拿起弓矢與長矛加入游擊。
causeEn: The causes are layered. The deepest is institutional: in 1809 Upper Peru was the economic heart of the empire, and neither Lima nor Seville could do without its silver and mercury, yet politically it remained a dependency of the Lima viceroyalty and of the Audiencia, with no representation of its own. In the reform wave of the four kingdoms at the end of the eighteenth century, Upper Peru was deliberately left out of reform, keeping only the right to petition the viceroy, never to decide its own fate. Administratively, in 1776 Viceroy Manuel de Amat carved the Potosí region out of Chuquisaca's jurisdiction and made it an intendancy, and the Chuquisaca bourgeoisie concluded that its territory and its courts had been stripped away; that resentment is the direct fuse of 10 May. The short-term trigger was the collapse of the Spanish monarchy: Napoleon's invasion in 1808 pushed the old royal house out, creole elites formed loyal kingdoms and swore to the Bourbons, and the viceroyal government itself was badly divided over the question of allegiance, as the revolt of the Lima merchants at Abancay in November 1808 showed when it was put down by force and several men were executed. That failure destroyed confidence in the viceroy's government among the elites and the people of Upper Peru alike. Last came the structural grievances: the silver mines depended on the mita, which every year pulled thousands of young men off the highland villages, and the Chiriguano and Guaraní settlements faced pressure over land and resettlement. So when the news of the rising reached the mountains, those communities took up bows and lances and joined the guerrillas without hesitation.
impact: 對當時，玻利維亞的起義把上秘魯從帝國的產出地變成了帝國的爭奪地。西班牙王室在鎮壓之後作出的回應，是一八一〇年四月二十一日與二十九日的王室詔令設立大河之普拉塔王室法庭，並把征服本管轄區的權力交給該法庭本身；這滿足了要求自治的商業菁英，卻仍未給上秘魯與其他各省一個席位。所謂第四個印加王國的方案被提起過，最終未成，爭端因此延續。軍事上，皇家軍在永加斯與奇查斯山區對加入起義的契里瓜諾與瓜拉尼部落的清剿，使高原邊緣的部落武裝在很長時間內失去獨立的戰鬥力；拉巴斯方面，執政會成員在一八一〇年五月被處決，其首腦被斬首陳示，鎮壓的規模本身成為新一輪動員的理由。長期看，一八〇九年的兩次革命把三樣東西留了下來：市議會奪權並宣稱代表人民效忠王室的合法性、地方原住民民兵與部落游擊網、以及把礦山與白銀視為本地權力基礎的群眾。一八〇九年之後的一八一〇年五月革命、馬德普拉塔的制憲會議、乃至一八二五年玻利維亞建國時對銀礦國有化的堅持，線索都能在這一年找到源頭。
impactEn: For the time, the Bolivian rising turned Upper Peru from a source of revenue into a contested frontier of the empire. The Crown's reply after the repression was a pair of royal cédulas of 21 and 29 April 1810 creating the Audiencia of the Río de la Plata and entrusting the conquest of its own district to that Audiencia; this satisfied the commercial elites who had wanted autonomy but still gave Upper Peru and the other provinces no seat of their own. The proposal of a fourth kingdom of the Incas was raised and not carried, and the grievance therefore ran on. Militarily, the royalist sweep through the Yungas and Chichas mountains against the Chiriguano and Guaraní communities that had joined the rising stripped the tribal fighters of an independent military role for a long time; in La Paz the members of the junta were executed in May 1810, their leader beheaded and displayed, and the very scale of the repression became the reason for the next mobilisation. In the long run the two revolutions of 1809 left three things behind: the legitimacy of a municipal council seizing power and declaring loyalty to the king on behalf of the people, the network of indigenous militias and tribal guerrillas, and the popular conviction that the mines and the silver were the basis of local power. The May Revolution of 1810, the constitutional congress in the Río de la Plata, and even the state nationalisation of the mines when Bolivia declared itself in 1825 all trace their threads back to this year.
result: 一八〇九到一八一〇年的第一階段以起義失敗告終：十月蘇克雷斯的執政會被皇家軍攻陷，十一月與十二月的蒙特雷與聖維森特兩戰，起義軍在開闊地屢遭砲火與騎兵打散；一八一〇年五月拉巴斯執政會垮台，成員被處決，第一共和國結束，佩內總督府恢復直接統治。然而失敗並不等於無果：這一年證實了兩件事，一是沒有野砲、騎兵與後勤，起義民兵無法在高原正面對決；二是單靠城市的群眾暴動守不住任何地方，必須有山區游擊與道路控制配合，兩者同時做到的地方，如永加斯與查奇亞，才真正拖住了皇家軍。整場玻利維亞獨立戰爭打到一八二四年才收尾，玻利瓦爾與蘇亞雷斯率解放軍自委內瑞拉翻越安第斯山，八月二十四日胡寧之戰取勝，十二月九日阿亞庫喬擊潰皇家軍，紅河與阿普里馬克河之間的平原上決定了最後勝負；一八二五年八月六日蘇克雷斯在玻利維亞宣布國家成立，玻利維亞的國旗、軍制與軍徽沿用至今。回頭看，野砲這種可拆成車體、能跟上隊伍的火砲，正是從一八〇九年到一八二四年壓在起義方頭上的一道門檻：誰掌握馬匹、砲組與道路，誰就決定高原戰役的節奏。
resultEn: The first phase, 1809 to 1810, ended in defeat for the insurgents. In October the Chuquisaca junta was stormed by royal troops; in November and December the insurgents were broken in the open field at Monterrei and San Vicente by gun fire and cavalry; in May 1810 the La Paz junta fell and its members were executed, ending the First Republic and returning Upper Peru to direct viceregal rule. Yet defeat was not without fruit. The year proved two things: without field guns, cavalry and logistics an insurgent militia cannot stand a set-piece battle on the plateau; and an urban riot alone cannot hold ground, which is why the places that combined mountain guerrilla war with control of the roads, the Yungas and the Chichas, genuinely held the royalists up. The whole Bolivian war of independence was not settled until 1824, when Bolívar and Sucre led the liberating army from Venezuela over the Andes, won at Junín on 24 August and broke the royal army at Ayacucho on 9 December, the last battle being decided on the plains between the Río Grande and the Apurímac. On 6 August 1825 Sucre proclaimed the state in Bolivia, whose flag, uniform and military tradition run to this day. Looking back, the field gun that could be broken into cart bodies and keep pace with the column was precisely the threshold pressing down on the insurgents between 1809 and 1824: whoever held the horses, the gun crews and the roads set the tempo of the plateau campaigns.
